previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in a right trimalleolar ankle fracture and bilateral leg ulcers with cellulitis. She had a history of COPD, diastolic heart failure, diabetes, and polysubstance abuse. Shortly after admission, she developed hypercarbic respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. She was treated for suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia with vancomycin and piperacillin/tazobactam, and a course of steroids for COPD exacerbation. Due to difficulty weaning, she underwent tracheostomy placement on hospital day 17. She also experienced acute renal failure, likely prerenal from hyperglycemia, which improved with IV fluids; lasix and lisinopril were discontinued. Multifocal atrial tachycardia was managed with metoprolol. Her leg infection resolved with antibiotics, and wound care was continued. She was weaned to a trach collar, mental status improved, and she was transferred to extended care for ongoing rehabilitation and trach management.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with a past medical 
history significant for COPD, dCHF, AF/MAT, OSA on CPAP, DM 2, 
CAD admitted for mixed hypercarbic hypoxic respiratory distress. 

.
MICU Course:
Patient presented to the ED with SOB, and just before admission 
was noted to be somnolent with an ABG showing a hypercarbic, and 
possibly hypoxic resp distress, and was admitted to MICU for 
monitoring.  Patient with fluctuating mental status 
corresponding to patient's clinical breathing.  She refused ABGs 
for further workup of her resp difficulty (attempting to discern 
whether there was a hypoxic component), and refused NIPPV as 
well.  Patient's mental status waxed and waned dramatically 
overnight with stable oxygenation 90-94% on 1LNC. The patient 
was continued on nebs, prednisone 40 mg, and levofloxacin given 
her productive cough. Her mental status improved by day two of 
her hospital course, and she was called out to the floor. 
.
A conversation regarding code status was held with the patient, 
and she remains full code.
.
Brief Hospital Course while on CC7
.
# Respiratory distress - likely multifactorial, but given her 
initial presentation of productive cough, somlenence and 
hypercarbia, COPD was high on the differential. After she was 
sent from the MICU, this appeared to be resolved and her main 
issue at ___ was her chronic congestive heart failure and her 
hypercarbia from obesity/hypoventilation syndrome.  We continued 
her COPD treatment with albuterol and ipratropium.  In addition, 
she got one dose of 40mg prednisone before it became clear that 
her SOB was more related to her CHF and less to her COPD, so 
this was dicsontinued.   We gave her a 5 day course of 
levofloxacin, which she finished without complication.  We gave 
her IV lasix PRN (she responded well to 40mg IV lasix), and put 
her on a 1500 cc fluid restriction and she was -6L from 
admission.  We then switched her to PO lasix 60mg QD.  Physical 
therapy saw her and reported she was okay to go home as long as 
she used her walker while there.  We attempted to wean pt's O2, 
and she was satting 95% on RA.  However, we did an ambulatory O2 
saturation on her and she was satting 81-82% on RA and 87-89% on 
2L NC O2.  She was to be sent home with home O2, but per her 
assisted living facility she smokes in her room, so this was not 
possible.  We kept her and continued to diurese another 3L off 
her with 60mg PO lasix QD and the 1500cc fluid restriction, and 
upon repeat ambulatory O2 sat she only went down to 89% on RA at 
her lowest reading.  She was therefore able to be sent home not 
on home O2.  We kept her on the 60mg PO lasix (instead of her 
preivous 40mg home dose), as she will almost certainly not 
adhere to a fluid restriction at home.  We plan to have her chem 
7 drawn in 5 days, and sent to her PCP, as well as get every 
other day weights from ___ until it is clear that the 60mg PO 
lasix is not overdiuresing her.  Her discharge weight on 
standing scale was 128.6kgs.   
.  
# UTI - She was growing e-coli in her urine, sensitive to 
floroquinolones. So,   
levofloxacin (started for cough productive of yellow/green 
sputum, see above), while not usually used for UTIs, was used 
and should have provided adequate penetration and coverage.  She 
completed a ___nd remained asymptomatic 
throughout her stay with no dysuria or frequency. 
.  
# OSA - the refused CPAP multiple times while on the floor.  
When started on it in the ICU she repeatedly ripped it off.  
Realistically, she won't wear a CPAP at home, so there is little 
intervention we can do for her in the longterm on this issue, 
other than encourage her to use CPAP.  We had many discussions 
on how CPAP could help her breathing, but each time she refused 
to try it. 
.  
# DM 2 - We held pt's metformin while she was in the hospital 
and put her on a SSI.  We restarted her home metformin at ___. 
 
.
# Depression - we continued pt's abilify and fluoxetine. 
.  
# Polysubstance abuse - we started a CIWA scale initially but pt 
did not require benzos during this admission, so we discontinued 
it ___.  
.  
# CAD: Low suspicion for ACS, troponin negative x2.  So we 
continued pt's BB, ACE-I, and clopidogrel and started her on 
81mg ___ QD.   
.
